claims.text: On 4 November 2025 the US government was fielding questions about the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS amid a government shutdown.

The episode exposed the absence of a standing government scientific body able to speak to anomalous objects, the gap the UAP Science Advisory Council was announced across seven months later. Reasoning: the same scientist, Loeb, was the principal public voice in both episodes.

desc: On 4 November 2025, during a government shutdown, DefenseScoop reported that the US government was grappling with questions about the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS. It belongs on this board not as a UAP case but as a boundary case: the third confirmed interstellar object to pass through the solar system, tracked by civil and defence sensors, generating public questions about whether it was natural, and arriving at a moment when the agencies that would answer were furloughed. Avi Loeb - who seven months later would convene the UAP Science Advisory Council - was the principal scientific voice in that debate, as he had been for 1I/'Oumuamua. The episode establishes the specific institutional gap the Science Advisory Council was later formed across: an anomalous object in the public eye, a government with the sensors, and no standing scientific body chartered to say anything about it.
